data.name: McpInstructions
data.value:
QueryCat exposes its function library (built-in functions plus functions from loaded plugins) as MCP tools. Use it for data transformations: string, date/time, math, JSON, encoding, and similar.
Workflow: 1. Call `search_functions` with a few keywords, e.g. {"term": "date truncate"}. Each word is matched against function names and descriptions. Results include `name`, `description`, `signature` and `relevance`; name matches rank higher. If nothing fits, try synonyms. 2. Read the `signature`, e.g. `substr(target: string, start: integer, count?: integer): string`. `?` marks an optional argument and `= value` shows its default. A function may have several overloads with different argument types. 3. If function's return type is `Object<IRowsInput>` or `Object<IRowsIterator>` call `execute_query` tool, f.e. "SELECT * FROM function_name()". For "FROM" use functions calling format (`SELECT * FROM get_users` must be `SELECT * FROM get_users()`). 4. Otherwise call `call_function` with the exact `name` and `args` as an object keyed by argument name, e.g. {"name": "substr", "args": {"target": "hello", "start": 1, "count": 3}}. You can leave out optional arguments.
Notes: - Aggregate functions such as sum or avg cannot be called. - In safe mode only read-only functions are allowed. - Errors come back as a tool result with isError=true and a message. Fix the arguments and retry. - The result is returned as {"result": value}. Integer, Float, Numeric and Boolean are JSON numbers/booleans; String, Timestamp, Interval and other objects are strings; Array and Map are JSON arrays/objects. - Functions returning `Object<IRowsInput>` or `Object<IRowsIterator>` return a table: {"columns": {"id": {"type": "integer"}}, "rows": [{"id": 1}, {"id": 2}]}. At most 1000 rows are returned.
